notes: Interpreted locally: type inferred, DOF=9, gripper=parallel.
metadata.source_prompt: Build me a movie-accurate wearable Iron Man Mark 43 suit from Age of Ultron with all the small polygon armour plates that open and close, repulsors, a HUD and an IMU. Budget $60000

design.summary: Iron Man Mark 43 (full wearable suit): 70 printed pieces, 4.0 kg filament, motorised faceplate, $257 incl. filament

uses: LM2596 5 V for servos and LEDs
webbing straps closing the split shells

checks.name: clearance:motion
checks.detail: no interference over 0 combined poses at the joint limits

assumptions: Joint limits trimmed to the collision-free range found by exact solid sweeps: left_elbow [-2.40, 0.00] -> [-1.82, 0.00]; left_hip [-1.90, 0.40] -> [-1.53, 0.40]; left_knee [0.00, 2.20] -> [0.00, 1.86]; right_elbow [-2.40, 0.00] -> [-1.82, 0.00]; right_hip [-1.90, 0.40] -> [-1.53, 0.40]; right_knee [0.00, 2.20] -> [0.00, 1.86].
padding gap 14 mm, PLA/PETG walls 3 mm, 15 % gyroid infill (shells are mostly walls)
the suit is worn armour: the wearer moves every joint; nothing powers the limbs (hobby servos cannot move a person)
wearer proportions from standard segment ratios scaled to the stated height; check against your own measurements before printing
